patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I rolled my ankle jogging on a curb — it's swollen and sore on the outside, but I can limp on it a little. No numbness or anything.
presentation.triageNote: 24-year-old female who rolled her ankle stepping off a curb. She has lateral ankle swelling and tenderness but can take a few weight-bearing steps; distal movement, circulation, and sensation are intact.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 5 is appropriate because this stable low-risk ankle injury can bear weight and is not expected to need imaging or another counted emergency resource.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This is an uncomplicated lateral ankle injury with preserved weight-bearing and intact distal function.
clinical.acuityReason: The low-risk mechanism and ability to take several steps make fracture less likely; no deformity or neurovascular compromise is present.
keyFindings: Rolled ankle stepping off a curb
Can bear weight for several steps
Intact distal movement, circulation, and sensation
teachingPoints: Validated ankle rules can reduce unnecessary imaging when their criteria are applied correctly.
Increasing pain, inability to bear weight, numbness, color change, or progressive swelling should prompt reassessment.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Supportive care, activity guidance, and return precautions would usually allow discharge without imaging.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated, one shoe off, ankle propped
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character. Match the painterly STYLE of the attached reference image - its brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting and palette - but do NOT copy its cropping, camera distance or composition. FRAMING (follow exactly): a full-body WIDE SHOT, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, subject centred. The ENTIRE figure must be inside the frame from the top of the head to the soles of both feet, and the ENTIRE chair must be inside the frame including all four chair legs meeting the floor. Leave clear empty margin on all four sides - roughly 10% of the image width as space above the head and below the feet. This is NOT a close-up, NOT a bust, NOT a head-and-shoulders portrait, NOT a cropped view: the camera is pulled well back so the whole person and the whole chair sit comfortably inside the picture with room around them. Draw the COMPLETE body - head, neck, torso, both arms, both hands, lap, both legs, both feet with shoes. Nothing cropped by the edges, no missing or truncated limbs, no body part fading out or left unfinished. ANATOMY AND OBJECTS (critical): exactly one head, exactly two arms ending in exactly two hands, exactly two legs ending in two feet, five fingers on each hand. No extra, duplicated, floating or partial limbs anywhere. Anything the character touches must be plausibly held by one of those two hands. All furniture is solid and fully opaque - the chair must never look transparent or see-through, and its back, seat and legs must all be completely drawn. Subject: a white 24-year-old woman in running clothes, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: one shoe off, ankle propped up. Expression: a mild wince, otherwise relaxed. Clearly visible: a swollen outer ankle. No text, no logos.
